target_customer: Hardware engineering teams in aerospace, robotics, automotive and related fields doing electrical and avionics system design
problem: Electrical system design for complex hardware is done in fragmented tools. Artifact offers a collaborative, version-controlled ECAD environment that generates diagrams, pin tables, harness drawings and BOMs from one system definition.
business_model: B2B SaaS for engineering teams (pricing not found)
product_category: ECAD and electrical systems design software with AI copilot

founders.name: Antony Samuel
founders.background_notes: YC page: electrical engineer with eight years in avionics and aerospace software.

founders.name: Corbin Klett
prior_employers: Aerospace industry, high-speed aircraft prototype (employer not named on YC page)

competitors.name: SnapMagic Copilot (SnapEDA)
competitors.what: AI copilot for electronics and circuit board design

competitors.name: Flux
competitors.what: Browser based PCB design with AI copilot that reads datasheets (vendor claim)

technical_complexity.rationale: Hierarchical, version-controlled ECAD with auto-generated manufacturing drawings and datasheet parsing is substantial engineering, aimed at systems rather than PCBs.

defensibility.rationale: Design data and workflows stored in the tool create lock-in once adopted by aerospace teams, but legacy ECAD vendors and AI-first rivals compete.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition or response found through the search.

market_need_then: Aerospace and defense hardware startups were scaling quickly in 2024 and 2025 and relied on manual harness and wiring documentation. The company shows logos from many such customers on its site.

branding.domain_note: Uses artifact.engineer, a non-.com domain; YC slug artifact-2 shows another YC company already took artifact.

identity.visual_style: minimal layout with bracketed section labels
identity.voice_and_tone: technical and direct, tagline Electrical systems, redesigned

branding.brand_signature: Bracketed section labels on the site
branding.community_and_virality: A Mastra blog describes it as Cursor for hardware; no other community evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: The name is generic and shared with Instagram's former news app and other firms; search results are crowded. Little brand press was found.

outcome_analysis: Artifact is active and small. The founders come from avionics and aerospace work, a good fit for the target buyers, and the site shows many aerospace customer logos. It announced a 3.5M seed in August 2025. No shutdown or acquisition was found. Competition from AI-first and legacy ECAD tools remains.
notes: Investors Floodgate and Boost VC come from a search summary of a podcast transcript and the Mastra blog; amount and date come from the YC page. Some aggregators list $5M or $5.1M with GV, likely a different company, and one lists $500K; ignored. Customer logos and usage numbers are company claims. Competitor dates are not tightly tied to the batch.
